intro.text: This is Odisha, over on the east side of India, right beside the Bay of Bengal. A bay is a wide curve of sea, and this one washes along the edge of Odisha for hundreds of kilometres. West Bengal is one of its neighbours. Its main city is Bhubaneswar, and Bhubaneswar is full of old stone temples.

animal.text: The Indian roller sits on a wire looking plain and brown. Then it opens its wings and flashes bright blue, as if a piece of the sky had gone flying past.

food.text: On hot days people here eat pakhala. It is cooked rice left sitting in water until it goes cool and a little bit sour. Fried fish goes on the side.

festival.text: At Rath Yatra, three enormous wooden chariots are built new every year. Thousands of people take hold of long ropes and pull them slowly down the road.

hello.text: In Odisha people say Namaskar. You put your palms together in front of you and dip your head a little as you say it. Try it now.

line.text: The whole temple is carved to look like a giant chariot. Twenty-four great stone wheels stand along its sides, and stone horses lean forward at the front. Guides here show you how the shadow creeping across a wheel tells the time, like a clock made of rock.

The tower of this temple is as tall as a building with twenty floors, so you can see it from right across the town. Behind it is one of the largest kitchens in the world. Cooks pile clay pots on top of one another over a wood fire and feed thousands of people.

Chilika is an enormous shallow lake where river water and sea water mix together. Dolphins live in it, with round heads and hardly any nose at all. When the cold months come, birds arrive here in their thousands, and some of them are pink.

The sand here is soft and golden and the waves come in long and loud. People build huge sculptures out of that wet sand, big enough to walk all the way around. Then the sea creeps up and takes every one of them away again.

They cut these little rooms straight into the hill with hammers and chisels, which are metal tools for splitting stone. Monks lived in them. A monk is someone who gives away all he owns and lives very simply. Two stone elephants guard one of the doorways.
